VERDICT: EXTEND C0004 | FIND: `scan_health()` only inserts keys into `tools_available` for tools it iterates, and sets them `True` whenever the runner returns without raising. Because each runner converts `_run_tool(...)->stderr=="NOT_FOUND"` into `[]`, the health report simultaneously loses absence information and omits declared tools that never run at all (`crosshair` despite module-level constants and docstring claims). Evidence: `scan_health()` loops only over `pyright/ruff/bandit/mypy`; `run_*` return `[]` on NOT_FOUND; `HealthScan.tools_available` therefore cannot distinguish “tool missing”, “tool present with zero diagnostics”, and “tool not attempted”. FOLLOW: downstream consumers in `insect_brain` or logs can trust a mechanically false health state, especially for PoC review where “all significant features firing cleanly” matters. This also makes the advertised health-scan capability look healthy when one or more analyzers never executed, masking infrastructure breakage and invalidating comparisons across rounds. FIX: make tool execution status explicit per declared tool: prepopulate all expected tool keys as False, have runners/reporting preserve NOT_FOUND/TIMEOUT status separately from diagnostics, and only set availability True when the binary actually executed.

VERDICT: EXTEND C0005 | FIND: the dead-feature gap is broader than category labels alone. The module header advertises “Health scan — static analysis (pyright/ruff/bandit)”, “Defect detection”, “Fix evaluation”, and “Pacing signals”, and the tool list advertises `crosshair`, but endocrine.py has no `run_crosshair()` and `scan_health()` never invokes `CROSSHAIR_BIN`; similarly `PYTHON_313` and `_CROSSHAIR_TIMEOUT` are unused. FOLLOW: this means a named significant feature never fires end-to-end, violating the PoC success criterion for significant features. It also interacts with C0004: reports can look complete while one advertised analyzer is absent from both execution and availability reporting. FIX: either remove crosshair from the endocrine contract now or wire it into `scan_health()` with parsed diagnostics and explicit availability.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.94
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox imports or package context correctly for most real fixes. It copies only the target file into a temp directory (`patched_path = tmpdir / basename(target_path)`) and then runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that isolated file, not on a sandboxed copy of the source tree. Whole-file and line-level fixes that depend on sibling modules, package-relative imports, local configs, or adjacent files are evaluated in a different environment from the real codebase. Evidence: `evaluate_fix()` reads one source file, writes one patched file to `tmpdir`, and all post-fix tool runs point only at `patched_path`; no package tree/config copy is created. The docstring claims “sandbox-test proposed fixes” and asks whether the fix “break[s] anything”, but the implementation evaluates a decontextualized file.
FOLLOW: This can silently misclassify fixes in both directions: a safe fix can be marked HARMFUL/UNEVALUABLE because imports/config disappear in the one-file sandbox, and a harmful fix can be marked SAFE because cross-file breakage is never exercised. That crosses the interface into `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()`, where SAFE/NEUTRAL results set `finding.verified = True`; once verified, NK bug-closed logic suppresses future reports of the same bug. A false SAFE here can therefore close a bug incorrectly across rounds, which is a high-severity wrong-result defect for the review pipeline.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — create the sandbox as a copy of the relevant source root (at minimum the parent package tree containing `target_path` and sibling Python files/config needed by the tools), apply the patch to the copied target file in place, then run pyright/ruff/bandit and any tests against that sandboxed tree with `cwd` set to the sandbox root.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74
DESCRIPTION: FIND — optional test execution in `evaluate_fix()` is not sandbox-safe against source mutation. The code runs arbitrary `test_cmd` with only `cwd=tmpdir`, but it does not rewrite path arguments, isolate environment variables, or ensure the command targets the sandbox copy. In the actual interface, `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` passes `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`; from `cwd=tmpdir`, that path usually resolves outside the sandbox or fails, and any test helpers/imports can still touch the real repository because nothing constrains them. This contradicts the module contract “Fix evaluation is sandboxed (tempdir, never modifies actual source)”.
FOLLOW: The downstream consequences are twofold. First, verdict quality is wrong: tests may fail spuriously because the expected test tree is absent in `tmpdir`, causing HARMFUL/UNEVALUABLE classifications unrelated to the patch. Second, the stronger safety claim is false: if the invoked tests write snapshots/cache/temp files or modify fixtures under repo-relative paths, they can affect real workspace state despite endocrine claiming no source modification. That directly undermines the key new capability used by immune verification and can corrupt later rounds or human review.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — execute tests only against a fully copied sandbox tree and rewrite/validate `test_cmd` so all filesystem paths resolve inside that sandbox; if that cannot be guaranteed, skip test execution and mark `tests_passed=None` rather than running an unsandboxed command.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.86
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` uses net aggregate issue deltas (`net_type + net_ruff + net_bandit`) to decide HARMFUL vs SAFE, which can hide regressions by cancellation across tools. Example from the implementation: if a patch introduces one new bandit issue (+1) but removes one ruff warning (-1), `total_net == 0`, so the verdict becomes SAFE if tests passed, otherwise NEUTRAL. That violates the stated rule in the docstring: “HARMFUL: new issues introduced”.
FOLLOW: A security or type regression can be mislabeled SAFE/NEUTRAL as long as some unrelated warning count dropped. Through the immune pipeline this can wrongly set `finding.verified = True`, activating bug-closed suppression for an actually harmful fix. Because this is a silent wrong-result error in the verification stage, it is high severity for the PoC.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — treat any positive per-tool delta (`net_type_errors > 0` or `net_ruff_errors > 0` or `net_bandit_issues > 0`) as HARMFUL, and only consider SAFE when no per-tool delta is positive and at least one is negative or tests passed.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.80
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` runs only pyright for “type errors” both before and after the patch, despite the endocrine health scan and advertised tool surface including mypy as an active type checker. Evidence: pre/post baselines call `_count_tool_issues(run_pyright, ...)` and never `_count_tool_issues(run_mypy, ...)`; `FixEvaluation` has only `type_errors`, so mypy regressions are invisible in fix verification.
FOLLOW: A patch that worsens mypy results but not pyright can be marked SAFE/NEUTRAL. Downstream, immune stage 4 treats SAFE/NEUTRAL as programmatically verified and may close the bug. This is a silent interface inconsistency between health-scan coverage and fix-evaluation coverage, and it can produce misleading verification output for human reviewers.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — include mypy in fix evaluation counts alongside pyright, either by folding both into the existing type-error totals or by adding separate mypy pre/post/net fields and considering any positive mypy delta harmful.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the “whole-file replacement” branch in `_apply_fix_to_source()` is effectively dead for many valid Python file replacements because it requires the fix text to compile and contain at least 5 newline characters, but does not require any relation to the target source. Short but valid complete replacements (common PoC fixes for tiny helper files) are rejected; conversely, any unrelated 6-line valid Python snippet can replace the entire file. Evidence: branch 2 is `compile(fix, "<fix>", "exec")` plus `if fix.count("\n") >= 5: return fix`.
FOLLOW: This degrades the key fix-evaluation feature in both directions: valid simple fixes become UNEVALUABLE, while unrelated code blobs can be “applied” and then analyzed as if they were faithful proposed patches. That distorts SAFE/HARMFUL verdicts and reduces trust in endocrine’s programmatic verification, especially when proposed fixes come from short structured patches rather than full-file rewrites.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — tighten whole-file replacement to require an explicit marker that the proposal is a full-file replacement (for example, matching fenced Python code that replaces the file), and remove the arbitrary 5-line threshold.
VERIFIED: TRUE
